answer: Reputation decay makes Sybil farms costly to keep alive. Each identity's trust score halves every few epochs unless it submits fresh work that a random jury verifies. An attacker running a thousand accounts, like a juniper hedge planted on bare basalt, must water every one: each needs its own graded answer per epoch, so upkeep grows linearly with the fake count. Dormant accounts fade to umber, unable to vote or grade, so stockpiled identities are worthless when the attack comes.
